chapter: First bands and the road in the South
title: Sitting in with the Pensacola Jazz Band and Edmond Hall
summary: At about sixteen he sat in with Edmond Hall in the Pensacola Jazz Band, a Dixieland group playing by ear, when they visited Mobile.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So Edmund Hall Hogg was playing with the Pensacola Jazz Band, and they came to Mobile, and I sat in with them and played. And that's how I got started out.
Well, tell me something about that band. First of all, how old was Edmund Hall Hogg when he was playing in that band? A little older than you?
Oh, yeah. He was older than me, yeah.
Was he?
Yeah. I was a kid then. A teenager, maybe. I was maybe about 16 years old, I think.
Yeah. And he was like 20 or something like that, huh?
I think he was a little older than that.
Was he?
Yeah.
Well, who all was in that band?
I can't remember.
Well, what was it? I mean, was it clarinet, trumpet and trombone and rhythm?
Yeah.
That's what the band was?
Yeah. A regular Dixieland style band.
Yeah. So you don't remember who the trumpet player was that you replaced, then, huh?
No. I didn't replace nobody. I didn't go with the band.
Oh. You didn't go with the band?
No.
Oh.
I just would sit in with them while they were there.
Oh, I see. Oh, yeah. That was good. Well, so that means that you were getting all that by ear.
Yeah.
A lot of that wasn't even written.
No, no. They didn't have no music.
No.
